subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / photovoltaics
motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka showed that organometal halide perovskites absorb light and generate photocurrent in solar cells. In 2012 Park demonstrated stable solid-state perovskite cells with efficiencies near 10%. In the same year Snaith discovered that the perovskite itself transports charge over long distances, which made meso-superstructured and planar thin-film architectures possible. Together these results created a new class of semiconductors that can be processed from solution at low temperature. They combine strong absorption, a tunable bandgap, long carrier diffusion lengths and unusual defect tolerance. Within a decade, single-junction efficiencies went above 26%, and perovskite-silicon tandems passed 33%, beyond the single-junction limit of silicon. Commercial tandem modules are now being produced. This is a physics discovery that has opened a new field of optoelectronics and is of great use to humanity, offering a practical route to cheaper and more efficient solar electricity.
